newsitem.title: UK: UK Lib-Dems put education top of election agenda.
newsitem.headline: UK Lib-Dems put education top of election agenda.

text.p: The centre-left Liberal Democrats on Monday put education at the top of their election agenda and challenged Britain's two main parties to match their pledge to raise taxes to pay for better schools.
Tony Blair, leader of the main opposition Labour party, has also vowed to make education his top priority if, as polls suggest, he wins the election on May 1.
But Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown blasted Blair for his party's timidity in refusing to consider spending more public money to raise school standards.
"All around the country, parents and teachers are up in arms about the cuts in their schools. They will rightly blame the government."

"But they should recognise that the Labour party will do nothing to help, because Labour have accepted the Conservative budget," Ashdown said in remarks prepared for delivery to the Jewish Board of British Deputies later on Monday.

He said the Liberal Democrats, which have 26 members of parliament in the 651-seat House of Commons and about 13 percent support in national opinion polls, would do something concrete to make Britain "the world's number one learning society in the next century".
Ashdown said the Lib-Dems would make sure that no primary school pupils were in classes of more than 30 and would guarantee nursery education to all three- and four-year-olds.
He also promised extra cash for books and equipment to all schools. The Lib Dems have said they would raise income tax by one percentage point to meet the bill.
"Today I challenge the other parties to match these commitments, to show that they, too, are ready to make the next five years the Parliament of Education'," Ashdown said.
